rationale: A codegen test's expected baseline offset changes from a rule-of-thumb constant to a derived one. CSS half-leading is single-reference: within a line box of height L carrying ink of height ascent + descent, the baseline sits at (L - ink) / 2 + ascent. The previous expectation, 11.7, was 1.5 + 0.85 * 12 -- it measured the surplus against the em box and then descended by a real face ascent, double-counting the difference between the two references. The corrected expectation, 12.2139, measures the surplus against the same ink the baseline then descends by: Inter at 12px carries 17.162109px of ink, so a captured 15px line box has negative half-leading (-1.081) and the glyphs overflow it evenly, which CSS permits. This reaches design-source-ingest only through the test/test_design_import_codegen.cpp path selector. No importer, no DesignIR schema, no capture format, no codegen emitter and no source-contract changes; the only edit is the numeric expectation and the derivation comment that explains it. The captured 15.0 line box in that fixture is hand-authored rather than a real Chromium capture, which is why the old constant survived. Registered as watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector without changing what the family proves. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.
